notes: The external LED and 220 ohm resistor are optional in the manual (the board has a built-in LED on pin 13). The graph includes them because the circuit image shows them.

Breadboard hole positions are read from the image. The LED's longer leg (anode) is the bent leg in column 6, and its shorter leg (cathode) is in column 8. The resistor spans columns 3 to 6 in row h (top half). The orange wire from pin 13 ends in column 3. The black wire from the LED cathode column 8 goes to the Arduino GND pin next to AREF. Rows h/g/f/i/j in the image are mapped to the catalogue's top-bank rows c/d/e. This is an approximation.
The USB cable is implied by the tutorial because the board receives serial data from the computer. It is not drawn in the image. Its ports are left unspecified because the catalogue entry has none.
The catalogue lists three GND ports, GND.1 to GND.3. The image shows the GND pin next to AREF on the digital header, which I mapped to GND.1.
The image shows both wires from the Arduino running to the breadboard. The black wire is routed over the top of the breadboard and into column 8, row g/h.
